transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, thanks for seeing me. I guess… I’m here because I’ve been having a harder time keeping my head on what I’m doing. It’s probably not anything too dramatic, but at work, like when I’m doing inventory, I’ll lose track or forget what I went to the supply closet for. And I’ve been trying to study for a supervisor certification, and I catch myself reading the same line over and over and not really taking it in. I just figured I should ask someone if that’s… you know, something to be concerned about.
Have you always had some trouble focusing, or is this something that’s gotten noticeably worse recently?

I mean, I’ve never been perfect with focus, I guess, but this feels more noticeable lately. Not like I can’t function or anything, but my head just doesn’t stay on task the way it should. Like with inventory, or when I’m trying to study for that supervisor certification, I’ll keep reading the same line and realize I didn’t take any of it in. Or I’ll go to the supply closet and then blank on what I went there for. It’s… embarrassing, honestly.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood lately, like feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but most days there’s kind of this heavy, flat feeling that follows me around. Like even when I’m just pushing my cart down an empty hallway at work, or sitting with my family and trying to act normal, it’s still there. I can still do things, but… I guess I haven’t felt very up, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed that you don’t take as much pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, time with family, or other activities?

I’m… not totally sure. I wouldn’t say I don’t enjoy anything anymore, exactly. I still show up for family stuff and I can get through things. Maybe it takes a little more effort to feel into it, if that makes sense, but I don’t know if I’d call it losing pleasure. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed that you feel more tired than usual or that you're lacking energy, even if you haven't done much physically or mentally?

I don’t know… not in a clear way, I guess. I mean, I get tired like anybody after work, but I haven’t really been tracking whether it’s more than usual. Some days I feel kind of worn down, but I don’t want to say it’s a big problem if it’s just normal life stuff, you know? Is that the kind of tired you mean?
Would you say that you feel depressed most of the day, nearly every day, or is it more that you have low moments that come and go?

I guess… it’s more most days than just little moments. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I still do what I need to do, but there’s usually this heavy, flat feeling kind of hanging around for a lot of the day. Like at work, pushing the cart down the hallway, or even at home with my family trying to act normal… it’s still kind of there. Is that what you mean?
Can you think of something that used to bring you enjoyment — even small things — and whether you still feel that same sense of enjoyment when you do it now?

Um… I’m trying to think. I mean, I still do little things I like, but I don’t know if I’ve really compared it that closely. Like, I don’t want to say I don’t enjoy them, because that sounds stronger than what I’m sure of.

Maybe some things feel a little more muted than they used to, but I’m not sure if that’s just being busy or tired from regular life. I guess I’d have to pay more attention to it. Is that an okay answer?
Can you think of a specific activity or moment — even a small one — that used to bring you a sense of enjoyment or satisfaction, and whether you still feel that way when you do it now?

I’m not sure I can name one clearly. Like, I used to maybe feel good after getting the apartment cleaned up or watching something with my family, but I don’t know if I’ve really stopped to notice whether it feels the same now.

I don’t want to overstate it. It might just be normal stress or being tired. I guess sometimes things don’t hit the same way, but I’m not sure I can give you a definite example. Is that still helpful?

Can you think of a specific activity or moment — even a small one — that used to bring you a sense of enjoyment or satisfaction, and whether you still feel that same sense of enjoyment when you do it now?

I’m sorry, I know I kind of didn’t answer that very clearly.

I guess… I still can’t think of one specific thing where I’m like, “Yes, that used to feel great and now it doesn’t.” It’s more vague than that for me. Like maybe everyday stuff feels less satisfying sometimes, but I don’t know if I’ve really paid attention enough to say for sure.

I don’t want to give you a wrong answer just to be helpful. Is it okay if I say I’m not really sure?
Can you think of any activity, even a small one, that you used to enjoy doing, and whether doing it now feels the same or different in terms of how much you enjoy it?

I’m sorry, I know I’m probably making this harder than it needs to be.

I honestly can’t think of a solid example. Like, there are things I do that are fine, and maybe sometimes they feel a little flat, but I don’t know if I’d say they’re actually different from before. I just haven’t really tracked it that way.

So… I guess my answer is I’m not sure. I can try to notice it more if that would help.
Can you think of any activity — even a small one — that you used to do that brought you some sense of pleasure or satisfaction, and whether doing it now feels any different in that regard?

I wish I had a better answer. I’m trying to think of something specific, but nothing really stands out clearly.

I do things like watch a show or get something done around the place, and sometimes it’s okay, maybe a little satisfying, but I don’t know if I can honestly compare it to before. I don’t want to say it’s different if I’m not sure.

Maybe I just haven’t been paying close enough attention to it. Is that an okay answer?
Can you think of a time in the past week when you did something you used to enjoy, and whether it felt as satisfying or pleasurable as it used to?

I’m trying to think of this past week specifically… and I’m still kind of blanking, sorry.

I did a couple normal things, like watched something for a bit, but I don’t know if I’d say it was something I “used to enjoy” in a clear way, or if it felt different. It was just… fine, I guess. Not bad.

I don’t want to overstate it or give you an answer that sounds more certain than I am. I’m honestly not sure I noticed enough to compare. Is that okay?
Over the past few weeks, have you found yourself not caring to do things you used to look forward to, even a little bit?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way exactly. I don’t think I’ve noticed myself deciding not to do things because I don’t care about them.

It’s more like… I just do the usual stuff, and I haven’t really thought about whether I’m looking forward to it or not. Maybe that sounds vague, sorry. I don’t want to give the wrong impression.

I guess I’d say I haven’t noticed that clearly over the past few weeks.
Over the past two weeks, have you found yourself not being interested in things you used to enjoy, even a little bit?

I don’t know… I’m having a hard time saying yes to that clearly. I haven’t really noticed myself thinking, “I don’t care about this anymore,” or anything like that.

Maybe I’ve just been kind of on autopilot, doing the normal things. If there’s been a difference, it’s subtle enough that I’m not sure I can point to it. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Is that the kind of answer you mean?
Can you think of a recent time when you did something you used to genuinely enjoy, and whether you felt the same level of enjoyment when you did it this time?

I’m sorry, I’m still not coming up with a clean example. I know that’s probably not very helpful.

I’ve done normal things recently, like putting something on to watch or just passing time, but I don’t know if I’d call it “genuinely enjoy” the way you’re asking. It wasn’t awful or anything… it just didn’t stand out enough for me to say whether it was the same level of enjoyment.

I guess the honest answer is I haven’t really noticed it clearly. Does that make sense?
Over the past two weeks, have you felt a lack of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even for a little while?

I think… I still can’t say I’ve really noticed that in a clear way. Like, I’m not sitting there thinking I don’t enjoy anything anymore.

Maybe things feel kind of ordinary, but I don’t know if that’s the same as a lack of interest or pleasure. I don’t want to overstate it just because you’re asking. So I guess my answer would be… not really, or at least I’m not sure. Is that okay to say?
Over the past two weeks, have you felt like you weren’t interested in anything or didn’t get any real pleasure from things, even the little stuff, most days?

I don’t think I’d say “most days,” no. Or… at least I haven’t been noticing it that strongly.

I still do little things to pass the time, and it’s not like I feel absolutely nothing from them. Maybe it’s a little muted sometimes, but I’m not sure if that’s what you mean. I don’t want to give the wrong impression and say yes if I’m not really sure.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, even if you were still able to go through the motions at work or at home?

Yeah… I think that one is probably more true than I want to admit.

I can still get through work and do what I’m supposed to do at home, so part of me wants to say it’s not that bad. But most days there’s this heavy, kind of flat feeling that just follows me around. Like even if I’m just pushing the cart down an empty hallway at work, or sitting with my family and trying to act normal, it’s still there.

I don’t know if I’d call it “nearly every day” exactly, but… most days, yes. Does that answer it okay?

I still do little things to pass the time, and it’s not like I feel absolutely nothing from them. Maybe it’s a little muted sometimes, but I’m not sure if that’s what you mean. I don’t want to give the wrong impression and say yes if I’m not really sure.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a persistent low mood that meets criteria for a major depressive episode, which would support F32.0 (Mild Depressive Episode) over F43.20 (Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood).
doctor.question: Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, even if you were still able to go through the motions at work or at home?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days I feel like there’s this heavy, flat feeling following me around, even when I’m just pushing the cart down an empty hallway or sitting with my family and trying to act normal.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking whether the patient has felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day, which matches depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think that one is probably more true than I want to admit.

I can still get through work and do what I’m supposed to do at home, so part of me wants to say it’s not that bad. But most days there’s this heavy, kind of flat feeling that just follows me around. Like even if I’m just pushing the cart down an empty hallway at work, or sitting with my family and trying to act normal, it’s still there.

I don’t know if I’d call it “nearly every day” exactly, but… most days, yes. Does that answer it okay?

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's chief complaint or reason for seeking help
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient endorses persistent depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks, in the absence of significant functional impairment or trauma-related symptoms. There is insufficient evidence for a diagnosis of adjustment disorder with depressed mood due to lack of a clearly defined psychosocial stressor or for psychotic, manic, or other mood symptoms.
